headline: High: LangGraph’s shared checkpointer and broad write/network capabilities can cascade into Plano’s logs/metrics and create default data-leak and coordination risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can write/read application files and shares state via a checkpointer store; Plano consumes config.yaml and OpenAI-compatible chat inputs. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in shared state or files can influence downstream prompts. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes persist untrusted text into shared checkpointer state
IF Plano reads that shared state or config-derived content into prompts without sanitization
mitigations: Separate shared state from prompt-bearing fields
Add allowlist parsing for any file-fed prompt content
Strip instruction-like text before passing data between agents
Use per-agent namespaces in the checkpointer store
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application-defined files and handles model provider API keys; Plano exposes logs, metrics, and traces and sends data to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If they share a workspace or checkpointer-backed state, sensitive graph state can flow into Plano’s telemetry or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same workspace or checkpointer store
IF Plano logs or forwards request payloads containing LangGraph state
mitigations: Keep LangGraph state and Plano telemetry in separate stores
Redact secrets before any outbound API call
Disable verbose request/response logging in Plano
Restrict shared filesystem access to read-only where possible
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction on graph state

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and browser capabilities; Plano has broad network egress and an OpenAI-compatible API surface. Even without explicit git/OAuth overlap, both can mutate shared application state or files if co-located, so coordination conflicts are plausible in default orchestration setups. Uncertainty about the shared workspace pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application directory or config path
IF one agent updates files while the other reads them concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Make shared config read-only during runs
Limit LangGraph tool nodes to least privilege
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework that can emit structured outputs from nodes, while Plano is an AI gateway/proxy that routes chat completions. If Plano treats LangGraph-produced content as authoritative routing or policy input, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or model calls. Because this interaction is undocumented and could affect many requests, high is warranted.
conditions: IF Plano uses LangGraph output as routing or policy input without verification
IF LangGraph nodes generate facts that Plano forwards to downstream systems
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Plano acts on LangGraph output
Require schema validation on all inter-agent messages
Log and review a sample of routed decisions
Use explicit confidence thresholds for automated actions
requires-engineering: add human approval for high-impact routes

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph touches model provider API keys and application-defined graph state, while Plano stores logs, metrics, and traces and routes data through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If regulated or sensitive data enters the shared pipeline, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two systems. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in graph state or routed prompts
IF Plano retains logs or traces longer than the source system
mitigations: Classify data before it enters either agent
Disable or shorten retention for logs and traces
Avoid sending secrets through Plano
Document residency and retention for both systems
requires-engineering: add policy-based data loss prevention
